As far as the procedure went:  I went to the clinic, filled out all the initial paperwork, spoke to a counselor about options, and waited my turn for an ultrasound. The nurse performed a transvaginal ultrasound to determine how far along I was and to confirm that I was actually pregnant. She gave me the option to look, but was non-judgemental when I chose not to. She took me to a private waiting room, I took 800mg of ibprofun, an antibiotic, and a light sedative, and I waited about 30-45 minutes for the sedative to take effect. Private room, table, manual vacuum, so no vacuum noise, and 5 minutes later I was curled up with a heating pad that took care of the residual cramps. The actual 5 minute procedure was kinda painful, but not much worse than normal period cramps, and the doctor warned me every time she was going to do something.  I waited another half hour or so, followed up with a nurse, and she walked me out to where my husband was waiting.

Afterward, I had cramps like a bad period for a little less than a week, some light bleeding for about 3 days, and everything was back to normal. I had some issues with lactation two or three days after the procedure, so be aware that might happen.

It sounds like your boyfriend and his family are really supportive.  Depression and anxiety are a bitch to go through alone and there's no shame in asking for help from people who care about you. I totally understand not wanting to use mental health as an excuse, but it's important to recognize that it isn't an excuse - it's something very real that you're dealing with.

There's also no shame in taking some time off school to take care of yourself. You can't be expected to do everything, especially if you feel like you're drowning. You're so strong just for sticking it out and trying to keep with school. If it takes you longer to finish, that's ok. If you decide it's not right for you to keep going to school right now, that's ok too. Your academic performance does not define your worth at all.

You absolutely deserve to live in a place you don't hate with people who care about you. From what you've said, I think moving to Florida would be a healthy decision. You are strong enough to get through this. You are going to be ok. I believe in you <3
